rationale: Same region and 9 module boundaries as trial-77617c1424 (ResNetEmbeddings + all 8 ResNetBasicLayer sites, groups 3821cceac23fa97e5a55/5233e425bbe8203a4dc0/5eb0dee1d36938317bbe/c1271430eda49ac23557/9f7c0638f7c2fd3e7c50; IDs re-verified against the current discovery in targets.json), with the two concrete defects that failed quality repaired. Diagnosis of the prior failure from previous-feedback: max_abs_error 40.837 with 32000/32000 logits mismatched (100%) is a data-placement error, not FMA drift; the prior Triton kernels launched grid axis 1 as channel index c and computed the plane base c*(N*H*W), i.e. channel-major indexing, while a contiguous NCHW tensor is batch-major (element (n,ch,h,w) at (n*C+ch)*H*W + h*W + w), so every channel/batch pair was scrambled. Repair 1: the kernels now enumerate N*C output planes on grid axis 1; plane p covers the contiguous span [p*H*W,(p+1)*H*W) and indexes the packed affine vectors by channel = p % C. Repair 2: the prior stem guard required x.shape[1]==num_channels(3) AND x.shape[1]==channels(64) simultaneously (coverage evidence: 'parent_fallback_guard' x2, reference_invocations 683c...x2), an unsatisfiable condition that made the stem silently fall back; it now checks the input against num_channels and the conv output against the BN size, so the stem actually fuses. Conv1/conv2/stem conv/stem MaxPool2d/shortcut conv+BN stay on the observed parent module dispatch (cudnn kernels, bit-identical outputs); each chain then runs one Triton kernel, y=max(fma(x,a,b),0) and y=max(fma(z,a2,b2)+s,0), with a=weight*rsqrt(var+eps), b=bias-mean*a packed once at installation. CPU validation of this attempt (no GPU touched): the kernels under TRITON_INTERPRET match torch relu(a*x+b) and relu(a*z+b+s) bit-exactly including a channel-mapping canary the old bug fails, and a full-model walk of the real pretrained weights through build()'s replacements reproduces the parent logits to 3.8e-06 max abs (tolerance 1e-4) with equal argmax and all 9 sites reporting fused routes. Expected effect (from the selection's measured composition: 88 forward kernels sum 4152.3us vs 4.2250ms median, so GPU-bound with ~73us host headroom; host-side plays and CUDA Graph replay stay rejected - replay would not rerun the Python hooks quality coverage counts): the 42 eager pointwise launches (20 BN 425.4us + 17 ReLU 343.9us + 8 add 120.4us = 889.7us) collapse to 17 single-pass kernels, cutting full-tensor traffic from 11 passes/block and 2 in the stem to 5 and 1, targeting the pointwise pool at ~380-450us and latency_ms 4.225 -> ~3.75-3.90ms (-8 to -12%), with the stem fusion now contributing rather than falling back. Numerics remain the same eval-BN affine the native cudnn bn_fw_inf_1C11_kernel evaluates, with only rsqrt/FMA ordering differences of ~1 ULP per element; final arbiter is the framework's paired logits check (atol/rtol 1e-4) and require_exact_top1 on the leased GPU.
setup_work: build() runs once at installation, before validation, on the modules from context['modules']. Per physical module: structural verification (Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU/Identity/MaxPool2d types, eval mode, affine BN with running stats), then one-time packing of eval-BN affine constants a=weight*rsqrt(running_var+eps), b=bias-running_mean*a for the 17 fused BNs (stem + 2 per block) as contiguous float32 device tensors computed under torch.no_grad from the live parameters: 34 tensors of at most 512 floats each, ~19 KB device memory total, retained for the module lifetime. Checkpoint parameters are never mutated (derived, detached copies only; verified by a parameter checksum in the CPU walk) and nothing fixture-dependent is precomputed. Triton JIT compiles lazily at first launch: 2 kernels x 3 BLOCK variants (64/256/1024 chosen per plane size H*W) = 6 compilations, landing in the framework's quality/coverage execution and the 2 warmup calls, ahead of the 5 timed samples; compilation is in-process cached and the timed window then launches only steady-state kernels. No CUDA Graph capture is used, so no retained graph pools are introduced and no invocation-boundary work is moved outside run(); Triton module loading is driver allocation outside the PyTorch allocator counters and no claim is made about it. Setup allocations and timing appear in the installation receipt.
quality_risks: FMA/rounding order differs from the native cudnn BN kernel and the separate add kernel by ~1 ULP per element (rsqrt(var+eps), fma(x,a,b) vs fl(fl(x*a)+b), and the (+s) rounding position); the full-model CPU walk measured 3.8e-06 max logit deviation, well under atol/rtol 1e-4, but the bound on GPU is confirmed only by the framework's paired logits comparison.

require_exact_top1: an argmax flip needs a top-2 logit gap below the fused drift (~1e-5 absolute); unlikely for the three pinned fixture images (CPU walk shows identical argmax), but it is a discrete failure mode only the GPU check can confirm.
tl.maximum(v, 0.0) maps NaN to 0 (IEEE fmax) whereas aten::relu propagates NaN; only relevant for non-finite activations, which the pinned finite FP32 fixture and weights do not produce.

Triton availability: triton 3.7.1 ships with the pinned torch 2.13.0+cu129 worker; if import or first launch fails, every affected call falls back to the parent forward via context['references'] with 'setup_fallback_parent'/'parent_fallback_error' route labels, preserving correctness at baseline speed; guard trips on unexpected signatures report 'parent_fallback_guard'.
First-invocation JIT compilation (6 variants, seconds) lands in quality/warmup execution outside the 5 timed samples; acknowledged as setup cost the framework observes.

The parent's in-place hidden_state += residual is replaced by an out-of-place fused write; this is alias-equivalent because the += target (the conv2-BN output) is block-local, never aliased outside the block, and the block input is read-only in both implementations (guard fallback result verified identical to the parent on CPU).

Peak allocated bytes may fall slightly because two fused intermediates replace five per-block temporaries; that is a per-run allocation-lifecycle counter change, not a general physical-memory saving, and setup adds ~19 KB of retained packed constants.
